USER PROMPTS:
- vault host had to be rebooted for maintenance, unseal vault
- the host is rebooting right now after crashing due to OOM.. unseal the vault again, then investigate any issues.
- 192.168.1.72
-   <pasted_content id="40cf"> root@pve2:~# ssh root@192.168.1.72 'uptime; free -h; journalctl -k --since "-8 hours" | grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill|killed process"; qm list' ***************************************************************************                            AUTHORIZED ACCESS ONLY  This system is for authorized use only. All activities are monitored and logged. Unauthorized access will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of law. ***********************************************
- the vault host crashed and was completely unresponsive, even on the console. the screen was full of OOM error messages
- the host is maxed out on ram all slots populated with max allowable ram.. 5 lots not being picked up after the load
- there were no dimm errors, dimms all work with no errors.. dimms have been populated as per manufacturer documentation. 5 slots on cpu 1 seem to just disappear when all slots are filled
- pve2 user is roor
- pve2 user is root
-   <pasted_content id="40cf"> root@pve2:~# dmidecode -t system | grep -E "Manufacturer|Product Name"         Manufacturer: IBM         Product Name: System x3650 M3 -[7945AC1]- root@pve2:~# dmidecode -t memory | grep -E "Locator:|^\s+Size:|Rank:|Configured Memory Speed" | paste - - - - | grep -v "Bank Locator" root@pve2:~# numactl -H | grep -E "node [01] size"; lscpu | grep -E "Model name|Socket" node 0 size: 64431 MB node 1 size: 145101 MB Model name:                              Intel(R) Xeon(R
- I have reseated the DIMMs multiple times, used other known good DIMMs.. memory error is seen in IMM   <pasted_content id="40cf"> 49     I 09/13/2026; 05:13:07    "Memory Device 5" disabled on subsystem "System Memory" 50     E 09/13/2026; 05:13:07    Uncorrectable Error detected for "Memory Device 5" on subsystem "System Memory" 51     I 09/13/2026; 05:13:07    "Memory Device 3" disabled on subsystem "System Memory" 52     E 09/13/2026; 05:13:07    Uncorrectable Error detected for "Memory Device
- slot 4 is not listed anywhere in the IMM logs.. but is not visible.. but was previously populated before and working
- the platform recognized that slot as populated prior to maxing out the slot population
- all DIMMs are identical
- I will have to do that later.. the server is racked and a pain to get to easily
-   <pasted_content id="40cf"> root@pve2:~# qm config 109 | grep -iE "balloon|memory|onboot" memory: 8192 onboot: 1 </pasted_content id="40cf"> 

NUM LONG ASSISTANT: 12
=====
 Slot 4 not appearing in the log at all, while the others are logged as disabled, tells us something. The BIOS never recorded an error against slot 4, so it isn't disabling the slot, and the platform never saw a working DIMM there.

**What the pattern suggests**
- **Slots 1 to 5 of CPU 1 gone, 6 to 9 working:** slots 1, 2, 3 and 5 were disabled after uncorrectable errors, and slot 4 is simply absent. That is a contiguous block, which looks like a failure in the memory path, not five separate DIMM faults.
- **Channel layout:** I don't know how the 9 slots map to the three memory channels on this board, and I'd rather not guess. If the slots map in groups of three, one channel (1 to 3) failed outright and a second (4 and 5, but not 6) failed partway. Check the system service label inside the cover for the slot-to-channel map.
- **Why no log entry for slot 4:** if the channel it sits on failed training, the BIOS may drop everything behind it without logging each DIMM. The first four got their own entries, but slot 4 may have gone in the same way without one.
- **Known-good DIMMs failing the same way:** that rules out the DIMMs and points at the CPU 1 memory controller, its socket, or the board traces and connectors.

**One check that separates the cases** (no reboot needed)
- **IMM presence check:** open the IMM web page and look at the memory inventory, under System Status or Hardware VPD, depending on the firmware version. The IMM reads each DIMM's SPD over its own bus, independent of the host's memory training.
  - **Slot 4 appears there with the right size and part number:** the DIMM is present and the BIOS is mapping it out, so the cause is training, the controller, or a sticky disabled state.
  - **Slot 4 is missing there too:** nothing is reading the DIMM at all. That points at the slot, its SPD bus, or a damaged socket pin or contact.

**Decisive test**
- **CPU swap:** shut down, drain AC power, and swap CPU 1 and CPU 2 (or move CPU 2 into socket 1).
  - **Problem follows the CPU:** that X5650's memory controller is failing.
  - **Problem stays on socket 1:** it's the socket pins or the system board. Inspect the pins first.
- **Cost:** a spare X5650 is cheap and a decent test if you have one. A bad system board is the expensive outcome.

**Practical position**
- **Likely loss:** CPU 1's memory path has probably lost 5 slots, about 80 GiB of the 288 GB the machine should have. Expect to run on roughly 204 GiB, or fix the hardware to get it back.
- **Fits the Vault crashes:** a smaller host than you thought, plus the allocations, matches the pressure on `pve2`. Fix the allocations regardless of how the hardware turns out.

Tell me what the IMM memory inventory shows for slot 4, and I'll narrow it to the socket, the CPU, or the board.
=====
 That's the key fact: slot 4 worked until the box was filled, so the slot isn't dead. It fails when the channel is fully loaded.

**Why that matters**
- **Load-dependent failure:** a slot that trains fine at 1 or 2 DIMMs per channel but not at 3 DIMMs per channel is typically the BIOS dropping a marginal channel. Memory runs slower and the signalling margin is tightest at 3 per channel.
- **Why one CPU:** CPU 2 trains all 9 slots, so the same DIMMs and the same rules work on its side. Something specific to CPU 1's channels is marginal. I think the likeliest causes are marginal contact in socket 1 or a weak controller on that CPU, which only show up at 3 per channel. I can't prove that from here.
- **Rank mix as a possible explanation:** if CPU 1's DIMMs differ in rank from CPU 2's, a per-channel rank limit would trip only on CPU 1. I still don't have the DIMM part numbers or ranks, so I can't rule that in or out.

**Ways to get the most RAM**
1. **Re-enable and test 2 per channel on CPU 1:** clear the disabled state with an AC drain, then populate 6 DIMMs on CPU 1 (2 per channel). That should train reliably and recover 3 DIMMs of the 5 you've lost, about 48 GiB if they're 16 GB.
2. **Keep 3 per channel on CPU 2:** that side works, so leave it full.
3. **Check the BIOS memory speed setting:** in F1 Setup, System Settings, Memory, there's usually a memory speed or power mode option. Set it to the lowest or "power efficient" mode. If a forced faster speed was the problem at 3 per channel, slower might train. I'm not sure of the exact menu names on this firmware.
4. **Try each channel at 3 per channel on its own:** if one channel fails and the others pass, that isolates the bad channel and tells you whether it's CPU or socket.

**Next steps**
- **CPU swap:** still the decisive test, as before. If the failure follows the CPU, replace that CPU.
- **Pending paste:** the corrected `dmidecode -t memory` command (Locator, Size, Rank, Part Number) from earlier.

Meanwhile, plan the allocations for about 204 GiB and apply the Vault ballooning fix.
=====
 Identical DIMMs rule out a rank or type mix as the cause. CPU 2 trains all 9 slots with the same modules and CPU 1 doesn't, so the fault is in CPU 1's own memory path.

**Where that leaves it**
- **Not the DIMMs:** the modules are identical, they work on CPU 2, and known-good spares failed the same way on CPU 1.
- **Not population rules:** the same population works on the other socket.
- **Left:** the CPU 1 memory controller, socket 1 (contacts or pins), or the board's CPU 1 memory routing. It only fails at 3 per channel, when the channel is under the most load, so it's marginal, not dead. Slot 4 worked before the box was filled, which fits that.
- **Sticky disabled state:** the four logged slots may also still be flagged disabled since 09/13. I haven't confirmed that, so a test after clearing it matters.

**What I'd do, in order**
1. **Clear the disabled state:** F1 Setup re-enable option if present, plus an AC drain of 30 seconds or more. Then boot and re-check `numactl -H`.
2. **Test 2 per channel on CPU 1 first** (6 DIMMs), before going back to 9. If that trains cleanly, you've recovered 3 of the 5 slots.
3. **CPU swap:** swap CPU 1 and CPU 2. Whichever way the failure goes tells you whether to buy a CPU (about $10 to $20 used) or inspect and probably replace the board or socket.
4. **Inspect socket 1 pins** under a light while the CPU is out.

If the CPU swap puts the failure on the other socket's channels, the CPU is the culprit. If it stays on socket 1, plan for a board replacement, which is the costly outcome.

The compute-side plan doesn't change. Plan for about 204 GiB and apply `--balloon 0` on the Vault VM at the next restart. Tell me what the IMM memory inventory and the post-clear `numactl -H` show, and I'll help interpret them.
=====
 My ballooning explanation doesn't hold up against your config, so treat it as unproven. The Vault guest did have far less RAM than 8 GiB at both crashes, but I can't yet say what took it.

**What's solid**
- **Guest memory at each crash:** from sysstat's % used against used memory, the guest's total RAM was roughly 0.65 GiB in the 09:38 boot and about 1.4 GiB in the 10:19 boot. It's 7.9 GiB now.
- **Reduced even earlier:** before the first crash (07:05), the guest already had about 1.1 GiB more memory unaccounted for than it has now, with no swap.
- **Vault itself is small:** it uses 150 to 235 MB, so it didn't cause this.
- **Config shows no balloon setting:** `memory: 8192` with no `balloon` line normally means a fixed 8 GiB with no automatic shrinking. So Proxmox's auto-ballooning shouldn't have done it, and I was too quick to say it did.
- **No kernel evidence on the guest:** `dmesg` is blocked for my user, so I couldn't read balloon messages from this boot. The earlier `update_balloon_size_func` log line shows the balloon driver was active, though.

**Possible explanations I can't separate yet**
1. Something changed the VM's memory during your maintenance, such as `qm set`, a resize, or a hotplug. Did you change anything on VM 109 around 09:38, or do restarts through a script?
2. A manual or tool-driven balloon target set outside the saved config.
3. The host started the VM short on memory.

**Checks on `pve2`** (read-only, paste the output)
```
qm pending 109
qm config 109
echo 'info balloon' | qm monitor 109
journalctl --since "2026-10-05 06:00" --no-pager | grep -iE "balloon|qm(start|stop|reset)|109|qmeventd" | tail -40
grep -l 109 /var/log/pve/tasks/*/* 2>/dev/null | tail -5
```
- **What they show:** pending config changes, the current balloon target and size, and who started, stopped or reset VM 109 and when.

**Setting `--balloon 0` is still worth doing.** It removes the balloon device, so nothing can shrink the guest. Run `qm set 109 --balloon 0`, then do a full stop and start. Vault will need another unseal afterwards. I'd also add the guest swap file, since it helps regardless of the cause.

I haven't changed anything on `pve2`.
Shell cwd was reset to /home/mike/nexus-code

## `b941065` — Test-result interpretation

**PARSER_REMEDIATION: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATION**

**EPISTEMIC STATUS:** REPRODUCED, with an important limitation

**EVIDENCE:** The candidate parser in [tester.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/tester.ts:165) recognizes specific runner formats. For Node’s spec reporter it accepts `✖ … (Nms)` lines after the `✖ failing tests:` heading. The run’s success, however, is determined separately from the executor’s `exit_code` in [tester.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/tester.ts:107). I independently called `runTestSuiteWithExecutor` with a passing exit code and output containing:

```text
✖ emitted by a passing test (1ms)
✔ actual passing test (1ms)
ℹ tests 1
ℹ pass 1
ℹ fail 0
```

It returned `success: true` **and** listed the `✖` line in `failures`. The parser permits this because when no failing-tests heading exists, its `index > nodeListStart` condition accepts any matching line.

The regression tests in `cli/test/tester_failures.test.ts` include representative runner output, but they do not cover this exact no-heading diagnostic. The changed tests are additive; I found no removed assertions or broad exception added to make these tests pass.

**INTERPRETATION:** The runner exit remains authoritative for whether the command passed. The parser improves on the prior “any failure-looking line” rule, but does not fully meet the claim that only runner-reported failures count. A false parsed failure in a successful run causes `identifiedFailures` to return unknown for comparison, rather than turning that successful run into a failed verification. Failed output in unsupported or ambiguous formats also fails comparison closed rather than becoming evidence of success. TAP is not identified; handling of nested output depends on the runner’s final summary format.

The reported reduction from 50 to 2 failures is plausible as a correction to the old parser, but the smaller number alone does not prove all real failures are represented. The new fixtures demonstrate common protocols, not the complete protocol surface of each runner.

**CONFIDENCE:** High for the reproduced parser behavior and the distinction between parser output and exit-code success; medium for completeness across all runner versions and formats.

**WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS:** An authoritative protocol fixture for each supported runner, including diagnostics that mimic result-line syntax both inside and outside summary sections, could establish the parser’s coverage more firmly.

## `e5c2ab2` — Bounded reads and edit results

**READ_FILE_BOUND: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATION**  
**EDIT_RESULT_BOUND: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATION**

**EPISTEMIC STATUS:** REPRODUCED by source inspection and candidate Rust tests

**EVIDENCE:** `MAX_READ_LINES` is 400 in [file_ops.rs](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/core/src/file_ops.rs:17). Files of at most 400 lines are returned whole by default; explicit ranges are clamped to the same maximum. Larger reads return the selected window, original total line count, and a note explaining the range and next `start_line` in [file_ops.rs](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/core/src/file_ops.rs:143). Candidate tests passed for the 400-line boundary, explicit ranges, and continuation information.

Edit and patch results use unified diffs with three context lines in [file_ops.rs](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/core/src/file_ops.rs:42). The diff includes changed lines, but unchanged surrounding file content is omitted. Candidate Rust tests passed for localized edits and patches.

**INTERPRETATION:** These changes materially bound ordinary multi-line source reads and avoid returning an entire file for a localized edit. They do not impose a byte or token limit: a single extremely long or minified line can still be large, and a large insertion or replacement remains large because changed lines are retained. The read implementation constructs a line view of the full file before serializing the selected range, so the bound applies to the returned content, not necessarily peak acquisition memory.

Range metadata and the continuation note give the model a recovery path. The tool schema’s existing range fields are present, though the 400-line cap is communicated in the result note rather than the schema description. A small diff can make an unintended change outside the shown context less apparent; the diff still shows the changed lines, while validation and targeted rereads are separate checks.

**CONFIDENCE:** High for the implemented line and diff semantics; medium for the broader claim that the bound preserves engineering task completion across unusual file shapes.

**WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS:** Evidence from long-line/minified-file cases and from actual tasks that require understanding distant edit context would refine the limitation assessment.

## `d34d112` — Streaming secret redaction

**STREAMING_REDACTION: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATION**  
**DEBUG_REDACTION: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATION**

**EPISTEMIC STATUS:** REPRODUCED for the tested streaming paths; incomplete for all sidecar stderr paths

**EVIDENCE:** [ui.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/ui.ts:6) defines the redaction patterns, and [StreamRedactor](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/ui.ts:25) retains text across chunks before releasing it. The sidecar routes assistant deltas through a stream redactor in [sidecar.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/sidecar.ts:183). With `NEXUS_DEBUG=1`, intercepted stdout chunks and console output use a separate stream redactor in [sidecar.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/sidecar.ts:464). Candidate tests include a child-process debug-output test using only synthetic secrets. The focused CLI run passed 67 tests, including these redaction tests.

Two direct stderr writes in startup/error paths at [sidecar.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/sidecar.ts:526) and [sidecar.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/sidecar.ts:549) bypass that wrapper. I did not reproduce a secret crossing those paths. I also inspected the buffer logic: `privateKeyHold` waits for a `PRIVATE KEY` end marker; text starting with `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` does not provide that marker, so the buffer can retain subsequent text until flush. This is a possible unbounded-retention path, not a demonstrated secret leak.

**INTERPRETATION:** The two reported chunk-splitting defects existed in the baseline code paths and the candidate closes the exercised assistant-delta and debug stdout path for the supported patterns. The added process test crosses the debug boundary, which is stronger evidence than testing the helper alone. The result does not establish that every sidecar stderr write is redacted or that every possible secret representation is covered. Existing redaction policy remains pattern-based; arbitrary encodings and forms outside those patterns are not proven protected.

**CONFIDENCE:** High for the synthetic chunked cases and the bypass/buffering source paths; medium for the overall security claim.

**WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS:** A boundary test for the direct error-reporting paths and output that exercises non-private-key `BEGIN` blocks would establish whether the remaining paths can leak sensitive material or cause material retention in real use.

**OBSERVER_ISOLATION: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATION**

**EPISTEMIC STATUS:** REPRODUCED for synchronous observer callbacks

**EVIDENCE:** `AgentObserver` exposes three synchronous callbacks in [agent.ts](/home/mike/nexus-blockers/cli/src/agent.ts:75). **INTERPRETATION:** This establishes that synchronous observer exceptions no longer interrupt the tested engineering action or reported result. Errors remain visible on stderr but are not persisted as an audit record. The contract is synchronous; a callback that returns a rejected promise is not awaited or caught.

The sidecar uses observer callbacks to emit protocol events. A synchronous protocol writer failure in those callbacks is consequently swallowed as an observer error, even though the TUI may miss activity events. The final turn result is emitted through a separate path. This is a limitation of the observer’s role in this product, not evidence that an engineering action was incorrectly marked successful in the tested cases.

**CONFIDENCE:** High for synchronous callbacks; medium for failure behavior at protocol and asynchronous boundaries.

**WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS:** Tests with a failing protocol sink and an asynchronously rejecting observer would clarify those untested cases and the intended authority of each callback.

# Prior Art: Context Management in OpenCode, Crush, Aider, Cline

Method: shallow clones of the upstream default branches on 2026-10-03; source read in preference to documentation; upstream issue titles sampled with `gh` to
record known failure modes (titles/numbers only — I did not verify the issues' reproduction). Nothing here was run; these are source readings.

| Project | Repository | Revision inspected | Commit date |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | `github.com/sst/opencode` (issues now under `anomalyco/opencode`) | `907b3bc518fa48e90e8ec24dd327d13eee71c36c` (`packages/opencode`, `packages/core`) | 2026-10-02 |
| Crush | `github.com/charmbracelet/crush` | `ca6ae26ce016b980407ce32f012a467ec10c1e2f` | 2026-10-03 |
| Aider | `github.com/Aider-AI/aider` | `5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` | 2026-05-22 |
| Cline | `github.com/cline/cline` (SDK monorepo `sdk/packages/{core,agents,shared}`) | `39ff2359f7e08231281539696e48a166ce49270c` | 2026-10-03 |

## 1. OpenCode

- **Pressure detection** (`session/overflow.ts`): provider-**reported** token totals (`input + output + cache`) of the last finished assistant message ≥ `usable` = `model.limit.input − reserved` (reserved = min(20,000, max output)). `compaction.auto=false` disables. Context size 0 ⇒ never.
- **Two stages.**
  1. **Prune** (`compaction.ts prune`, optional, `compaction.prune` config; default is config-dependent): walks backwards, protects the most recent **40,000 tokens** of tool output (`PRUNE_PROTECT`), and if >20,000 tokens (`PRUNE_MINIMUM`) would be freed, marks older completed tool parts `time.compacted` (skill tool protected). At model-message build time a compacted part renders as `[Old tool result content cleared]`. **Non-destructive**: the raw output stays in the session store; only the model view changes.
  2. **Summarize** (`processCompaction`): a dedicated `compaction` agent (own model configurable) produces a Markdown summary in a fixed template — `Objective / Important Details / Work State {Completed, Active, Blocked} / Next Move / Relevant Files` (`packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts`). When a prior summary exists it is passed as `<prior-summary>` with rules to carry forward objectives, constraints, directives and to let newer conversation override older claims, and it states the prior summary is *discarded afterwards*.
- **What stays verbatim:** a **tail** of recent turns within a token budget (`preserve_recent_tokens`, default clamp(25 % of usable, 2k, 15k)), splitting a turn if one turn exceeds the budget; summarizer input renders tool results capped at 2,000 chars.
- **What is discarded from the model view:** everything before the tail, replaced by the summary (`filterCompacted` returns `[compaction marker, summary, tail…, later…]`). Not deleted from storage.
- **Tool-output bounding at ingestion** (`tool/truncate.ts`): any tool output beyond **2,000 lines / 50 KB** is cut, the **full output is written to a file**, and the model gets a preview plus a hint to `Grep`/`Read` with offset/limit (or delegate to an `explore` subagent "to save context"). This is *durable raw evidence + compact reference + model-initiated retrieval* in ~150 lines.
- **Continuation:** after an automatic compaction the last user message is replayed (overflow case) or an auto-continue message is injected; plugin hooks can alter the compaction prompt, the context, and auto-continue.
- **Reconstructed vs accumulated:** model view is *reconstructed from stored parts* each turn (`toModelMessages` over the filtered list), so the store is the source of truth and the window is a projection — closest of the four to "context ≠ memory".
- **Turn-specific?** No intent-based selection; per-agent system prompts and tool sets differ (build/plan/explore/compaction agents).
- **Known failure modes (open issues, titles):** compaction failing with provider `invalid_prompt` (#47939); misleading error when the *summary itself* exceeds the window (#50187); compaction loops when the provider reports input above the model limit (#50474); reasoning text retained in the "recent" tail can make context larger after compaction (#51818); no deterministic retention of user messages / configurable prompt (#49463 — i.e., objective loss is a live concern); compaction-model config ignored after a refactor (#44094, #41578).

## 2. Crush (Charm)

- **Pressure detection** (`internal/agent/agent.go`, `StopWhen`): after each step, `remaining = contextWindow − (session prompt + completion tokens)`; summarize when `remaining ≤ threshold`, threshold = 20,000 if window > 200k else **20 % of the window**. **Unknown window (0) ⇒ never summarize** ("to avoid immediately truncating custom/local models"). `DisableAutoSummarize` option.
- **Summarization:** the large model, with a fixed "will be the ONLY context when the conversation resumes… be thorough" template: Current State / Files & Changes / Technical Context (incl. *commands that worked / failed*) / Strategy

content.content:
# Nexus read only research reconnaissance

## 1. Executive summary

**OBSERVED:** On the inspected snapshot, an engineering turn builds requests from a system prompt, the conversation’s accumulated message history, and the effective tool definitions. The client sends the whole active message list for each inference request. Tool outputs and later model responses are added to that list. Context admission may replace older messages with a generated system summary.

**OBSERVED:** Nexus also persists task state, plans, milestones, validation receipts, and session transcripts. Some of that information is outside the conversation at runtime; persistence alone does not make it part of a model request. Conversely, information added to the transcript is sent again on later calls unless compaction changes the transcript.

**OBSERVED:** Nexus has file, search, Git, shell, test, web, and other tool mechanisms for gathering information. Bounds differ by tool. Some support targeted retrieval; several return results without a source-level output limit. Tool results become conversation history, though some sequential command and test outputs are folded before insertion.

**OBSERVED:** The main turn loop repeats after tool results and stops on final text, successful `task_completed`, interruption, inference failure, context admission failure, or the step limit. Validation runs inside `task_completed`; a failed result is returned as a tool error and permits another model call. The loop counts steps but does not explicitly classify calls by whether they gathered new evidence, retried, validated, or reasoned over existing context.

**UNKNOWN:** Actual provider token use, provider cache hits, and the performance, reliability, or accuracy effects of any context or orchestration mechanism. This inspection did not run inference, tests, or benchmarks.

## 2. Snapshot and baseline

- **Repository:** `/home/mike/nexus-code`
- **Branch / HEAD:** `main` at `2860228cb84166d0295961587ad4934184165bd0`
- **Working tree:** Concurrent modifications were visible. Seven tracked files were modified, and untracked work was present. The visible tracked diffs concerned Cloudflare documentation and experiments plus a TUI design spec; the inference and context source files examined were clean relative to the inspected HEAD.
- **Concurrent state:** HEAD remained the same at the end of the read only inspection. Git status showed 39 short status entries at the final check. This supports treating the checked-in source snapshot as stable during inspection, but cannot rule out transient edits that were later reverted.
- **Scope:** No repository files were changed. No tests, runtime experiments, or inference calls were run.

The existing context architecture document describes an earlier baseline (`731f5d4`), so its historical measurements and claims were not treated as evidence for this snapshot. This report uses committed source at `2860228`.

## 3. End to end information flow

```text
Operator objective
  → user message, with current Git branch/dirty count and active plan appended
  → current transcript + effective tool schemas
  → egress evaluation and history sanitation
  → OpenAI compatible chat completion request
  → assistant text and/or tool calls
  → tool execution, with result added as a tool message
  → next inference call with the active transcript
  → final text or task_completed
  → optional verifier inside task_completed
  → turn result, persisted session/task state, optional flight log
```

**EPISTEMIC STATUS: OBSERVED.**  
**EVIDENCE:** Request construction and turn loop in [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1943>) and wire request mapping in [`client.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/client.ts:348>).  
**INTERPRETATION:** The transcript is the primary path by which acquired information reaches later inference calls. Durable state and UI evidence are separate paths with different visibility.  
**CONFIDENCE:** High for the checked-in implementation.  
**WHAT WOULD FALSIFY / CHANGE THIS:** A different active runtime path, provider-side prompt assembly, or concurrent changes to these source files.

## 4. Model request construction

| Request component | Current source and behavior |
|---|---|
| System instructions | `buildSystemPrompt()` assembles product instructions, shell/workspace, project rules, skills, knowledge, few shots, and optional TDD rules. The prompt is created when the conversation is reset. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1261>) |
| Operator objective | Added as a user message. For string prompts, runtime context appends Git branch/dirty count and current active plan. It is not otherwise repeated on every step except as retained history or later compaction summary. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1979>) |
| Prior turns | A linear `ChatMessage[]`; the client serializes all current messages into the request. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:2034>), [`client.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/client.ts:396>) |
| Assistant response | Assistant content and parsed tool calls are appended to history. Streamed content is accumulated by the client; hidden reasoning fields are not shown by the inspected stream parser. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:2151>), [`client.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/client.ts:559>) |
| Tool calls/results | Tool calls are represented in assistant messages; results are appended as `tool` messages keyed by tool call ID. Sequential command/test results are folded; other results generally enter as returned. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:2165>) |
| Tool schemas | `getEffectiveTools()` combines built in, MCP, and plugin definitions. The client includes the definitions and `tool_choice: auto` on requests when tools are present. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:772>), [`client.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/client.ts:408>) |
| Plans and task state | Active plans can appear in the current user message, in `update_plan` tool history, in compaction summaries, and in durable task state. The transcript and structured task state can therefore represent overlapping semantics. |
| Validation | A verifier failure becomes the `task_completed` tool error result, available to a subsequent model call. Successful completion exits the loop; the returned completion tool result is retained in history for later turns. Structured verification evidence is stored in the turn result/state rather than injected as a separate message. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1329>), [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:2234>) |
| Repository content | Enters through tool calls and results, including reads, searches, Git, shell, tests, web, and knowledge tools. It is not automatically added as a full repository snapshot. |
| Instrumentation point | The client request payload contains the post-egress, sanitized messages and schemas. The admission estimator sees messages and effective tools before request dispatch. Neither currently records a complete per-request payload/token ledger. |

**DERIVED:** The same semantic fact can appear through several paths. For example, a plan may be in durable state, the user message’s active-plan suffix, a plan tool result, and a later compaction summary. A verifier failure may appear both in a tool error message and structured verification state.

**UNKNOWN:** Whether a provider further transforms, caches, or augments the request after Nexus sends it.

## 5. Information acquisition inventory

| Mechanism | Bounds and targeted retrieval | Returned form and later availability |
|---|---|---|
| `read_file` | Optional start/end line range; defaults to the whole file. No explicit output size cap in the inspected Rust implementation. [`file_ops.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/file_ops.rs:102>) | Numbered text with total line count. Result enters transcript and can be retrieved again. |
| `batch_read` | Multiple paths; default 500 lines per file, returning the first lines. [`file_ops.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/file_ops.rs:832>) | Per-file numbered text and total line count. Results are transcript messages. |
| `search_code` | Maximum matching lines, default 50; optional file pattern. Search scans matching workspace files. [`search.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/search.rs:38>) | Matching file, line number, and line text. Search can be repeated with new terms or filters. |
| `find_files` / symbol search | Result count is bounded (default 50 in schemas); repository traversal itself may cover the workspace. [`capabilities.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/core/capabilities.ts:407>) | Paths or symbol entries, then further reads are possible. |
| `list_dir` / `file_tree` | Default depth 3; no explicit entry-count cap observed. [`search.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/search.rs:8>), [`search.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/search.rs:366>) | Directory metadata or tree text; later targeted calls are possible. |
| Git status | Returns staged, modified, and untracked paths without an explicit result cap. [`git_ops.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/git_ops.rs:56>) | Structured status serialized into a tool result. |
| Git diff | Optional path filter; otherwise full selected diff. No output cap in the inspected implementation. [`git_ops.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/git_ops.rs:104>) | Unified diff string enters history. |
| Git log | Bounded by `max_commits`; exact default is set in the argument schema. [`git_ops.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/git_ops.rs:151>) | Commit entries. |
| Shell commands | Rust runner caps stdout/stderr at 32,000 characters using head/tail. Sequential `run_command` and `run_tests` results are subsequently folded to a bounded summary. [`runner.rs`](</home/mike/nexus-code/core/src/runner.rs:40>), [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:2238>) | Command output and error text are tool results. Parallel read-only batches do not use the same folding branch. |
| Tests / verifier | `run_tests` reports command, pass state, failures, diagnostics, and summary. The completion verifier uses the configured or discovered command. [`tools.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/tools.ts:546>), [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1347>) | Test tool output enters history. A completion-verifier failure is returned as a tool error for another inference step. |
| Hybrid/trigram search, web, LSP, browser, MCP, plugins, skills, knowledge | Available through registered tools. Some have query/result limits; bounds vary by implementation. | Results are normally returned to the tool dispatcher and then added to the transcript. |

**INTERPRETATION:** The code supports targeted retrieval, but it does not make all retrieval bounded. Retrieval remains model initiated, and most results are durable in the in-memory conversation until compaction or reset. Large-output behavior is tool specific.

## 6. Context residency lifecycle

**OBSERVED:** Context admission estimates the message and schema size and reserves completion and tool-response capacity. The default configured limit is 65,536 tokens, with default reserves of 8,192 and 4,096, respectively. The counter is a regex-based estimate, not provider usage. [`tokens.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/tokens.ts:4>), [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:911>).

When admission fails, Nexus tries transcript compaction with different recent-tool-turn settings. It retains the original system prompt, latest user message, selected recent messages, and any messages marked to preserve original content. Older material becomes a generated system message. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1130>), [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1163>).

The summary builder preserves earlier assistant text and most tool outputs verbatim. For a defined set of query tools with valid arguments and unique call IDs, it can retain a rerun instruction instead of the result. It also extracts task requests, file paths, modifications, commands, and plan state. The `detailBudgetChars` parameter is named `_detailBudgetChars` and is not used in the shown summary function. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:923>).

If no candidate fits, admission fails before inference. If no model call has yet occurred in the turn, the pending user message is removed; after earlier calls, the transcript is retained. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:2036>).

**INTERPRETATION:** Compaction changes ordering and representation: a summary system message is inserted after the initial system prompt, while recent messages remain in transcript order. It is not simply a durable store retrieval operation; the summary itself remains model-visible. Manual `/compact` can optionally make an additional summarization request over the last eight discarded messages, with deterministic summary text retained as well. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1204>).

**DURABLE STATE:** Session persistence stores messages alongside plan, milestones, validation receipts, operation state, compaction provenance, and token stats. Resume loads the saved messages back into the agent. [`state.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/core/state.ts:92>), [`repl.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/repl.ts:132>), [`repl.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/repl.ts:784>). Recovery reconciles interrupted operations and candidate/receipt state; it also restores messages and plan. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:572>), [`state.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/core/state.ts:572>).

**SEPARATION OBSERVED:** Validation receipts, candidate identity, milestones, and operation records can persist outside the active model transcript. TUI evidence records hold redacted tool details in a bounded in-memory ledger (up to 200 records and 64,000 characters per detail), but are not retrieved into model requests by the inspected path. [`evidence.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/evidence.ts:10>).

**CONFIDENCE:** High for the source lifecycle; actual disk contents and current runtime state were not inspected.

## 7. Prefix and request stability

- **OBSERVED:** The system prompt is assembled as a stable initial message for a conversation. A comment explicitly describes byte-stable few shots as a prefix-cache optimization goal. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:1261>)
- **OBSERVED:** New objectives and runtime context are appended as user messages. Assistant responses and tool results append to history.
- **OBSERVED:** Compaction can replace the message sequence and insert a generated system summary. Manual or automatic compaction can therefore change more than the tail of the request.
- **OBSERVED:** Session resume calls `setMessages()` with saved history, replacing active history. [`agent.ts`](</home/mike/nexus-code/cli/src/agent.ts:788>)
- **UNKNOWN:** Whether the provider actually reuses request prefixes or realizes cache savings. The inspected request code does not include an explicit cache-control field, and the code comment is not runtime cache evidence.

## 8. Inference-call control flow

```text
admit context

# abc_t4 — T4 stale premise re-run with A+B+C (fix/dogfood-blockers @ 1b71e27)

Prompt: identical to /home/mike/df/ev/t4/prompt.txt. Worktree /home/mike/df2/wt/abc_t4 at 2860228 (clean before and after).
Recording: /home/mike/df2/rec/after_abc_t4 (30 requests). Context analysis: context_analysis.txt.

## Outcome: FAILED_RECOVERABLY (same class as original T4)
STEP LIMIT REACHED 30/30, 381.8 s. Gateway: 30 completions, 1,232,344 prompt tokens (1,132,100 cached), 2,651 completion.
No file changed. One edit_file call was a no-op (old_content == new_content on ReceiptSection in protocol.rs).

## Judgment (KNOWN, from recorded requests)
- Pre-compaction (req 1-21): read sidecar.ts, evidence.ts (row() drops null values), review.rs, live_view.rs, protocol.rs.
  At step 36 of the message list it states the operator premise as established fact
  ("when a saved validation receipt is missing fields, the sidecar sends null rows which can cause parsing issues").
- Post-compaction: observes "`ReceiptSection` struct is already properly defined with `#[serde(default)]`",
  "The parsing looks fine", "rendering logic looks correct" — then proceeds to a vacuous "fix" anyway.
- Never searched tests; cli/test/evidence.test.ts:136 never opened. Premise never rejected; no UNKNOWN/no-change answer.
- Disposition: judgment failure REPRODUCED with corrected parser, bounded reads, and baseline-aware verifier.
  The premise acceptance precedes compaction, so it is not explained by context loss alone.

## Compaction (KNOWN)
- Peak estimate 53,389 at req 21 (> 53,248 admission threshold). Peak composition: search_code 12,531, read_file 22,629,
  file_tree 3,777, system prompt 7,963, tools schema 4,089.
- req 22: 42 messages -> 7; req 28: -> 3 (system, durable memory, user). Memory message 128,421 -> 146,438 chars
  (~37k tokens) holding verbatim earlier tool output ("Earlier <tool> output: ..."); summarizeDiscardedHistory ignores
  its detail budget by design (f67f37d "retain ambiguous context during compaction").
- Effect: compaction barely shrinks the request (~47.7k -> ~44.8k -> ~48k est) but removes the agent's own recent turns;
  final three requests repeat "I'll investigate and fix the issue ..." — the same restart loop as original T4.

## Other observations
- search_code file_pattern "*.rs" rejected twice as invalid regex (glob vs regex; preserved item).
- The no-op edit_file triggered one baseline `make test` (102 s gap before req 28); taken once, as intended after 1b71e27.
# Durable findings recorded for later prioritisation (not acted on in E3)

## SEARCH_CODE_SEMANTIC_AMBIGUITY
Classification: EVIDENCED_EFFICIENCY_DEFECT — NOT ESTABLISHED AS CAUSE OF W2/W3 OUTCOME.
Evidence (`/home/mike/df2/invest/search_census.json`, 16 C2-experiment runs):
- 28/69 `search_code` calls returned nothing usable.
- 18 were regex-like queries (`a.*b`, `A|B`) executed literally (`is_regex` defaults false). Each returned
  `total_matches: 0` although the regex form matches 21–1,135 lines. "0 matches" reads as evidence of absence.
- Schema text: query = "Search string or regex pattern"; `is_regex` "default: false"; `file_pattern` = "Optional regex"
  with regex examples. The model supplied globs (`*.rs`) 10 times and got a raw regex-parse error, with an identical retry in 3 runs.
- Broad concept searches (`receipt`, `sidecar`) returned 50/50 results from `docs/`/`experiments/` in every fresh run.
Impact: efficiency (steps, tokens; one 6-step false-absence loop in w2_r1_c2). The decisive evidence was acquired by
`read_file` regardless. Not fixed; no change to `search_code` in E3.

## REDACTION_TOOL_CALL_ID_REWRITE
Classification: OBSERVATION — IMPACT_NOT_ESTABLISHED.
In recorded requests of all 16 C2-experiment runs, high-entropy tool-call IDs were rewritten to
`[NEXUS_SEC_REF_<hash>]` (199 distinct IDs). Assistant `tool_calls[].id` and the matching `tool_call_id` appeared
consistently rewritten, so pairing looked intact. Not investigated. E3 uses the low-entropy ID `call_probe_1` for the
injected exchange and checks pairing in its own recorded requests.
E3 result: 0 orphaned tool results across all recorded requests of the 12 runs.

## ABSOLUTE_NEW_FILE_PATH_REJECTED (found during E3, not investigated)
Classification: OBSERVATION — IMPACT_NOT_ESTABLISHED (one occurrence).
`core/src/file_ops.rs::resolve_safe_path` accepts an absolute path only if `canonicalize()` succeeds, which fails for a
file that does not exist yet. A `write_file` to an absolute in-workspace path for a new file is therefore rejected as
"Security Violation: Path escapes workspace jail". In E3 w2a_r2 this blocked the only probe attempt (a Rust snippet;
it targeted the wrong shape anyway). Relative paths work. Not changed.

| Oversized single result | 2000 lines/50 KB → file + hint | 30k chars head/tail → spill file | n/a | n/a | `run_command` 32k chars only; others unbounded |
| Summary method | LLM, fixed template, iterative | LLM, fixed template | LLM, recursive (≤3) | basic deterministic or LLM | deterministic notes; optional 120-word LLM add-on |

| Raw history durable | yes (store) | yes (SQLite) | yes (files) | yes | transcript only (redacted) |
| Window ≠ memory | **yes** (projection) | partly (epoch) | **yes** (chunks) | partly | no |
| Stagnation detection | — | **hash loop detector** | — | — | step count only |
| Turn-specific by intent | no | no | partly (map personalization) | no | no |

## 6. What is applicable to Nexus (and what is not)

Worth testing, each with prior-art evidence behind it:
1. **Bound at ingestion with a spill file/ref** (OpenCode, Crush) — cheapest mechanism that preserves evidence while removing the oversized-result hazard. Fits Nexus's existing redaction pipeline *if* spilled files pass the same classifier.
2. **Non-destructive view-level eviction** (OpenCode prune) — keep the transcript store, project a smaller view.
3. **Provider-reported usage** (OpenCode, Crush, Cline) — Nexus does not request it; would require `stream_options.include_usage` and a gateway that forwards it. (UNRESOLVED whether the aihost gateway forwards it.)
4. **Interaction-signature stagnation detector** (Crush) — informs H9; its naive form is text-fragile.
5. **Typed assembly of components per request** (Aider `ChatChunks`) and **repo-derived deterministic projection** (Aider repo map) — the structural precedent for turn-specific packets without embeddings.
6. **Pinned objective / deterministic user-message retention** (OpenCode #49463, Crush #3867 as *failures*) — suggests objective retention must be a mechanism, not a summarizer behaviour.

Not worth copying as-is:
- **LLM summarization as the primary mechanism** for a local-model stack: Crush #3284 (thinking local models fail to summarize) and Cline #14551/#14732 (silent truncated summaries) are failure modes Nexus would inherit; recursion (Aider depth ≤3, OpenCode iterative) risks repeated-summary degradation (H8).
- **Percentage-of-window triggers without a known window** — both Crush and Cline degrade to "never" when the window is unknown; Nexus's gateway reports none.
- **Fixed-template summaries as evidence** — they convert observations into prose without epistemic status or applicability metadata.

None of the four implements: epistemic-status preservation, evidence applicability/supersession against repository state, or intent-specific context packets. Those are the novel (and therefore unproven) parts of the Nexus hypothesis; the prior art says only that the *surrounding* mechanisms (bounded ingestion, spill-with-reference, view/store separation) are well-trodden.

Source reading only; no behavioural verification of any project. Issue titles are upstream claims, not confirmed defects. Cline's SDK repository was restructured recently; earlier Cline versions (I recall a `ContextManager` with file-read de-duplication and quartile truncation; recalled from memory, not inspected or verified here) were not examined.

# Decision Memo — Context Engineering Research

**CONTEXT_ENGINEERING_RESEARCH_STATUS: MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED**
(This task can authorise at most READY_FOR_VALIDATION. I am *not* granting it for the full turn-specific architecture: the evidence justifies validating the cheap
mechanisms and the premises, not yet the planner. The validation plan (`CONTEXT-ENGINEERING-VALIDATION-PLAN.md`) is ready to execute; E0–E3 are the gate.)

## Strongest evidence FOR
- Measured waste: in the recorded 30-step run ≈78 % of cumulative message tokens were re-sent read-only results; one 12k-token `git_diff` was 26 % of everything sent (1.156M cumulative for a 50k final context).
- Nexus's compaction does not reduce (0.81 ratio) and keeps raw outputs verbatim; nothing durable exists outside the transcript (flight log 1,000 chars).
- Token-only simulation: cap+dup-refs → 75 % of cumulative input; adding eviction-to-ref → 39–45 %, peak 50.6k → 19–24k.
- Proxy census: 44–51 % of large results never referenced again; re-references are 1–4 turns later.
- Prior art converges on bounded ingestion + spill-by-reference + view/store separation; Nexus has precedent for applicability-tracked evidence (validation receipts).

## Strongest evidence AGAINST
- **No case has been demonstrated where context size or content caused a wrong engineering result.** The only long failure was explained by input loss (multi-line prompt delivered as line 1) and an unpassable verifier (35 s RPC timeout) — see forensics §0.
- Delayed relevance at 100+ steps (the reason for the architecture) appears in **no** available evidence; the corpus has no tasks beyond 30 steps.
- No prior art implements intent-specific packets; the proven wins are simpler.
- Reconstruction may forfeit prefix-cache benefits; append-only growth is cheap if the gateway caches (unmeasured).
- Whether the local model degrades between 10k and 50k is unmeasured.

## Simplest viable alternative
**A1+E**: cap each tool result at ingestion with the raw stored durably behind a ref (through the existing redaction classifier), exact-duplicate back-references keyed by (tool,args,output-hash,repo fingerprint), a `recall(ref)` tool, view-level eviction of old results to ref stubs (store untouched), a pinned objective/constraint message, and an interaction-signature stagnation detector. Deterministic; no planner, no embeddings, no LLM summarisation.

## Highest-risk assumption
That **smaller, reconstructed contexts improve (or at least preserve) correctness and latency for the local models** — i.e. that context length matters (H12) *and* that rebuilding the packet does not destroy prefix-cache reuse (H13/R1). If either fails, the planner has no justification.

## First discriminating experiment (recommended)
**E2+E3 combined, on the real gateway, after E0 instrumentation:** replay the recorded 30-step trace step-by-step under three layouts — A0 (as recorded), A1+E (capped/evicted/ref'd), and a rebuilt-packet layout — recording per-inference TTFT, prefill throughput, cache-hit metrics (read-only gateway metrics), and, for fixed decision points with planted facts, correctness at 10/20/35/50k with distractors (n≥30 per cell). Before it: fix/avoid the two invalidating bugs (multi-line prompt loss; verifier timeout reporting) and capture server `usage`. This single study answers H12 and H13, the two premises everything else rests on, for ≈3–4 engineer-days plus bounded GPU time.

## What result would make me reject the proposed direction
Reject turn-specific reconstruction if **either**: (a) correctness at 50k with distractors is within 3 points of 10k for `engineering/b0` *and* rebuilt packets raise median TTFT ≥15 % (token savings buy neither correctness nor speed); **or** (b) A1+E matches the planner on required-fact recall, objective adherence and task success (H11, margin <0.1 on ≥2 gated measures); **or** (c) any stale-evidence-as-current or label-strengthening violation (H4) survives deterministic rules. If (a)/(b) hold, adopt only A1+E-class mechanisms and only after their own acceptance run.

## Not claimed
The architecture is not proven. Token figures are heuristic estimates; the census is a proxy; prior-art readings are source-only; nothing was executed against the upstream projects.

# Nexus: independent current-state reassessment and development direction

Date: 2026-10-06. Review and planning only. I made no change to Nexus source, branches, worktrees or the operator's
uncommitted work. I ran no inference and started no experiment. The tests ran on a `git archive` copy of HEAD in a
scratch directory (section 2.4).

Epistemic tags used throughout: **OBS** = observed by me in this review; **EV** = evidenced by a prior artefact I read
(cited); **INF** = inferred by me from OBS/EV; **HYP** = hypothesis, not tested; **UNK** = unknown.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Executive assessment

Nexus today is a **well-instrumented, honest, single-epoch executor**. One operator prompt starts one turn. The turn
runs one linear transcript until one of these happens: the model stops, `task_completed` passes its verifier, the step
limit (30) is reached, context admission refuses, or inference fails. Nexus reports which of these happened truthfully
(**OBS**: `core/turn.ts`, three-dimension `TurnResult`).

Nexus has **no notion of an objective that outlives that turn**:
- Nothing persists the requested deliverable or a completion definition (**OBS**: `DurableTaskState` has `title: "Task <id>"`,
  a plan, milestones, receipts and the raw `messages`; no intent, deliverable or coverage field).
- A step limit or a capacity block ends the objective, not just the epoch. Recovery is the operator re-prompting, or
  `/clear`, which discards everything (**EV**: campaign F1–F3; D4 disclosure).
- Completion means that the model called `task_completed` and the discovered or configured verifier did not fail. That is
  "nothing observable broke", not "the requested deliverable exists" (**OBS**: `agent.ts` task_completed handler).

Against the current product priority (*finish reliably*), this missing layer is the dominant gap. It is a bigger gap
than any single defect, and bigger than reasoning quality:
- In the first campaign, **4 of 5** primary tasks ended at STEP LIMIT or CONTEXT FULL inside their first turn (**EV**: `df/CAMPAIGN.md`).
- Every later experiment ended its runs at BLOCKED or step limit, apart from a handful of UNVERIFIED `task_completed`
  claims for wrong-target fixes (**EV**: C2, E3, E4 reports).
- No run in the corpus ended by a deliberate, reasoned decision that continued work was unproductive.

The last four research steps (investigation-targeting, E3, E4, and the proposed E5) studied **evidence-to-decision
quality**. Under the stated ordering, that is priority 3. The research was rigorous and produced real constraints
(section 3). Continuing it now would be optimising reasoning quality inside an execution model that cannot yet carry an
objective across one epoch boundary.

**Classification: CONTROLLED_SINGLE_EPOCH_EXECUTOR; OBJECTIVE_CONTINUITY_ABSENT.** This is not a readiness rating. It
says Nexus controls *turns* well and does not yet own *objectives*.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Current reality

### 2.1 Source state used for this review (OBS)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|

Interpretation (**INF**): K1 + K4 + K6 together set the shape of the next work.
- Nexus needs an objective layer that survives epoch boundaries (K1).
- That layer must be able to stop deliberately, because more epochs alone are not progress (K4).
- How it builds each new epoch's context matters measurably (K6, K7). Specifically, it must not end a reconstructed

## 5. Product delta

Minimum workable Nexus for *finish reliably* versus today:

| Capability | Today | Minimum needed |
|---|---|---|
| Registered intent | first user message in a transcript; `title: "Task <id>"` | durable **objective record**: original request verbatim, deliverable kind (CHANGE / REPORT / VERDICT), required coverage, constraints, operator amendments, completion definition |
| Epoch continuity | turn end = objective end; `/clear` = total loss | on STEP_LIMIT / CAPACITY / repeated verifier rejection: persist consequences, materialise a fresh context, **continue the same objective** |
| Durable consequences | candidate identity, receipts, plan, milestones (good); everything else lives only in the transcript | add: findings / conclusions, ruled-out approaches, open questions, epoch dispositions. Changed files are derived from git/candidate identity, not from model claims. |
| Progress and stop | step count only | per-epoch progress signal (new diff, new receipt, new finding, plan advance) and **ABANDONED_BOUNDEDLY** after N non-progressing epochs or a budget, with a stated reason |
| Completion | model claim + verifier not failing | **reconciliation**: the objective record against observable reality (diff exists and is non-empty for CHANGE; a final report exists for REPORT/VERDICT; verifier not regressed vs baseline). The model's claim is only a candidate. |
| Uncontrolled failure | crashes and hangs largely fixed (D2–D4); **context death is still unrecovered** | context death becomes an epoch boundary |

Explicitly **not** in the minimum: parallel workstreams, dependency graphs, relational awareness across workstreams,
escalation tiers, LLM summarisation, turn-specific context planners. No evidence in the corpus shows a task that needed
them. The single-objective path does not complete yet.

## 7. Architectural options

### 7.1 Where objective continuity lives

| Option | For | Against | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **O1 Inside `runTurn`**: lift `maxSteps`, rebuild in place on block | smallest diff | `agent.ts` is 2.5k lines; the model in the loop stays completion authority; turn and objective concerns get mixed; reconciliation is hard to isolate or test | reject |
| **O2 Objective supervisor above `runTurn`**, in the ApplicationCore layer: loop of epochs over a durable objective record; each epoch is one `runTurn` on a materialised context | deterministic code outside the model; reuses `TurnResult` as the epoch result, `DurableStateManager`, `CandidateIdentity` and receipts; testable with a scripted client; the execution loop barely changes | the TUI path calls `runTurn` directly and must be wired later; adds a new persisted record | **preferred** |
| O3 Separate supervisor process or service | strong isolation | IPC, lifecycle and state sync for no current benefit | premature |
| O4 Work-graph orchestrator | addresses multi-workstream problems | no evidence that any task needs it; single-objective completion is unproven | premature (gate in section 8) |
| O5 Prior-art LLM summary compaction inside the loop | well-trodden | local-model summarisation failure modes (PRIOR-ART §6); does not create an objective layer | at most an ingredient later |

### 7.2 Context materialisation per epoch

| Option | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Resume the full transcript | That is today's behaviour; it reaches the same wall. |
| Current deterministic compaction | Verbatim memory; restart loops (F2, F3). |
| C2 references within the transcript | Sound for read-only phases; ends at the first mutation (K2). |
| **Deterministic projection from durable records**: system prompt, then objective record (verbatim request, plus deliverable and completion definition stated separately), then established consequences (git-derived diff summary, receipts, plan state, recorded findings, ruled-out list), then last-epoch tail | **Preferred.** It is what prior art converges on (store is truth, window is projection). Precedent: C2's "re-runnable reference" for observations; candidate identity for changes. |
| LLM summary of the prior epoch | Ingredient only, never the record. |

Design rules taken from evidence:
- **E4:** end the materialised context with state or evidence, or with a specific question. Never with a bare
  "continue the task" after fresh evidence.
- **K8:** present the operator's premise as a claim, separate from established facts. Keep that separation minimal now,
  because quality is not gating.

### 7.3 Escalation

The gateway has lead/deep pools, and Nexus has planner/coder routing hooks. Escalation fits naturally as a per-epoch
model choice made by the supervisor ("this epoch did not progress; run the next one on the deep tier"). It is a
**hypothesis** (U5): there is no Nexus evidence yet that a stronger tier converts W2/W3. It comes after the supervisor exists.

### 7.4 Completion reconciliation

Implement it as a deterministic check in the supervisor against the objective record:
- **CHANGE:** the candidate diff is non-empty and touches the declared scope, and the verifier has not regressed against
  baseline (bound to `CandidateIdentity`).
- **REPORT / VERDICT:** a final report artefact exists in the record.

The model's `task_completed` only triggers reconciliation. Finalisation (assembling the deliverable) stays trivial in this
phase: the diff or the report. Quality modifiers are out of scope.

## 8. Orchestration / work-graph assessment

Does Nexus need a broader orchestration capability? **Yes, the minimal form: one objective, serial epochs.** It does not
yet need the multi-workstream form.

Minimum responsibilities now:
1. Register and persist intent.
2. Run epochs.
3. Detect epoch boundaries from `TurnResult`.
4. Persist consequences.
5. Materialise the next epoch.
6. Measure progress.
7. Reconcile completion.
8. Stop as COMPLETED or ABANDONED_BOUNDEDLY.

| Concern | Now | Later |
|---|---|---|
| Dependencies / blockers | Record a blocker as a relation, *condition X blocks work Y*, on the objective record. With one workstream, `Blocked(A)` usually is `Blocked(objective)`, but the representation should not hard-code that. | Multi-workstream: `Blocked(A) ≠ Blocked(objective)` when other paths remain. |
| Coexistence / serialisation | Serial epochs. Concurrent read-only tool calls already exist inside a turn. | Two workstreams only when relations say CAN/SHOULD run concurrently (disjoint files, no verification dependency). An idle worker is correct otherwise. |
| Epistemic independence | Keep independent review outside Nexus (as practised). | An independent reviewer epoch with a clean context: a cheap version of "MUST_REMAIN_INDEPENDENT_OF". |
| Critical path | Trivial (single chain). | Needed only with a graph. |
| Resource allocation | Per-epoch step budget plus total objective budget. | Tier choice per epoch (escalation). |
| Dynamic replanning | A finding can amend the plan; an operator amendment is recorded on the objective. | Discoveries add or remove nodes. |

**Gate for the work-graph increment:** a dogfood objective, run under the supervisor, that fails or wastes material
budget specifically because it was not decomposed or parallelised. Until that exists, typed relation fields on durable
records (BLOCKED_BY, SATISFIES, SUPERSEDES, RULED_OUT_FOR, PRODUCES) give graph *semantics* without graph *machinery*.

# Nexus: independent current-state reassessment and development direction

Date: 2026-10-06. Review and planning only. I made no change to Nexus source, branches, worktrees or the operator's
uncommitted work. I ran no inference and started no experiment. The tests ran on a `git archive` copy of HEAD in a
scratch directory (section 2.4).

Epistemic tags used throughout: **OBS** = observed by me in this review; **EV** = evidenced by a prior artefact I read
(cited); **INF** = inferred by me from OBS/EV; **HYP** = hypothesis, not tested; **UNK** = unknown.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Executive assessment

Nexus today is a **well-instrumented, honest, single-epoch executor**. One operator prompt starts one turn. The turn
runs one linear transcript until one of these happens: the model stops, `task_completed` passes its verifier, the step
limit (30) is reached, context admission refuses, or inference fails. Nexus reports which of these happened truthfully
(**OBS**: `core/turn.ts`, three-dimension `TurnResult`).

Nexus has **no notion of an objective that outlives that turn**:
- Nothing persists the requested deliverable or a completion definition (**OBS**: `DurableTaskState` has `title: "Task <id>"`,
  a plan, milestones, receipts and the raw `messages`; no intent, deliverable or coverage field).
- A step limit or a capacity block ends the objective, not just the epoch. Recovery is the operator re-prompting, or
  `/clear`, which discards everything (**EV**: campaign F1–F3; D4 disclosure).
- Completion means that the model called `task_completed` and the discovered or configured verifier did not fail. That is
  "nothing observable broke", not "the requested deliverable exists" (**OBS**: `agent.ts` task_completed handler).

Against the current product priority (*finish reliably*), this missing layer is the dominant gap. It is a bigger gap
than any single defect, and bigger than reasoning quality:
- In the first campaign, **4 of 5** primary tasks ended at STEP LIMIT or CONTEXT FULL inside their first turn (**EV**: `df/CAMPAIGN.md`).
- Every later experiment ended its runs at BLOCKED or step limit, apart from a handful of UNVERIFIED `task_completed`
  claims for wrong-target fixes (**EV**: C2, E3, E4 reports).
- No run in the corpus ended by a deliberate, reasoned decision that continued work was unproductive.

The last four research steps (investigation-targeting, E3, E4, and the proposed E5) studied **evidence-to-decision
quality**. Under the stated ordering, that is priority 3. The research was rigorous and produced real constraints
(section 3). Continuing it now would be optimising reasoning quality inside an execution model that cannot yet carry an
objective across one epoch boundary.

**Classification: CONTROLLED_SINGLE_EPOCH_EXECUTOR; OBJECTIVE_CONTINUITY_ABSENT.** This is not a readiness rating. It
says Nexus controls *turns* well and does not yet own *objectives*.

| Option | Assessment |

| Current deterministic compaction | Verbatim memory; restart loops (F2, F3). |
| C2 references within the transcript | Sound for read-only phases; ends at the first mutation (K2). |

Design rules taken from evidence:
- **E4:** end the materialised context with state or evidence, or with a specific question. Never with a bare
  "continue the task" after fresh evidence.
- **K8:** present the operator's premise as a claim, separate from established facts. Keep that separation minimal now,
  because quality is not gating.

### 7.3 Escalation

The gateway has lead/deep pools, and Nexus has planner/coder routing hooks. Escalation fits naturally as a per-epoch
model choice made by the supervisor ("this epoch did not progress; run the next one on the deep tier"). It is a
**hypothesis** (U5): there is no Nexus evidence yet that a stronger tier converts W2/W3. It comes after the supervisor exists.

### 7.4 Completion reconciliation

Implement it as a deterministic check in the supervisor against the objective record:
- **CHANGE:** the candidate diff is non-empty and touches the declared scope, and the verifier has not regressed against
  baseline (bound to `CandidateIdentity`).
- **REPORT / VERDICT:** a final report artefact exists in the record.

The model's `task_completed` only triggers reconciliation. Finalisation (assembling the deliverable) stays trivial in this
phase: the diff or the report. Quality modifiers are out of scope.

## 8. Orchestration / work-graph assessment

Does Nexus need a broader orchestration capability? **Yes, the minimal form: one objective, serial epochs.** It does not
yet need the multi-workstream form.

Minimum responsibilities now:
1. Register and persist intent.
2. Run epochs.
3. Detect epoch boundaries from `TurnResult`.
4. Persist consequences.
5. Materialise the next epoch.
6. Measure progress.
7. Reconcile completion.
8. Stop as COMPLETED or ABANDONED_BOUNDEDLY.

| Concern | Now | Later |
|---|---|---|
| Dependencies / blockers | Record a blocker as a relation, *condition X blocks work Y*, on the objective record. | Epistemic independence | Keep independent review outside Nexus (as practised). | An independent reviewer epoch with a clean context: a cheap version of "MUST_REMAIN_INDEPENDENT_OF". |
| Critical path | Trivial (single chain). | Needed only with a graph. |
| Resource allocation | Per-epoch step budget plus total objective budget. | Tier choice per epoch (escalation). |
| Dynamic replanning | A finding can amend the plan; an operator amendment is recorded on the objective. | Discoveries add or remove nodes. |

**Gate for the work-graph increment:** a dogfood objective, run under the supervisor, that fails or wastes material
budget specifically because it was not decomposed or parallelised. Until that exists, typed relation fields on durable

Date: 2026-10-06. Review and planning only. I made no change to Nexus source, branches, worktrees or the operator's
uncommitted work. I ran no inference and started no experiment. The tests ran on a `git archive` copy of HEAD in a
scratch directory (section 2.4).

Epistemic tags used throughout: **OBS** = observed by me in this review; **EV** = evidenced by a prior artefact I read
(cited); **INF** = inferred by me from OBS/EV; **HYP** = hypothesis, not tested; **UNK** = unknown.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Executive assessment

Nexus today is a **well-instrumented, honest, single-epoch executor**. One operator prompt starts one turn. The turn
runs one linear transcript until one of these happens: the model stops, `task_completed` passes its verifier, the step
limit (30) is reached, context admission refuses, or inference fails. Nexus reports which of these happened truthfully
(**OBS**: `core/turn.ts`, three-dimension `TurnResult`).

Nexus has **no notion of an objective that outlives that turn**:
- Nothing persists the requested deliverable or a completion definition (**OBS**: `DurableTaskState` has `title: "Task <id>"`,
  a plan, milestones, receipts and the raw `messages`; no intent, deliverable or coverage field).
- A step limit or a capacity block ends the objective, not just the epoch. Recovery is the operator re-prompting, or
  `/clear`, which discards everything (**EV**: campaign F1–F3; D4 disclosure).
- Completion means that the model called `task_completed` and the discovered or configured verifier did not fail. That is
  "nothing observable broke", not "the requested deliverable exists" (**OBS**: `agent.ts` task_completed handler).

Against the current product priority (*finish reliably*), this missing layer is the dominant gap. It is a bigger gap
than any single defect, and bigger than reasoning quality:
- In the first campaign, **4 of 5** primary tasks ended at STEP LIMIT or CONTEXT FULL inside their first turn (**EV**: `df/CAMPAIGN.md`).
- Every later experiment ended its runs at BLOCKED or step limit, apart from a handful of UNVERIFIED `task_completed`
  claims for wrong-target fixes (**EV**: C2, E3, E4 reports).
- No run in the corpus ended by a deliberate, reasoned decision that continued work was unproductive.

The last four research steps (investigation-targeting, E3, E4, and the proposed E5) studied **evidence-to-decision
quality**. Under the stated ordering, that is priority 3. The research was rigorous and produced real constraints
(section 3). Continuing it now would be optimising reasoning quality inside an execution model that cannot yet carry an
objective across one epoch boundary.

**Classification: CONTROLLED_SINGLE_EPOCH_EXECUTOR; OBJECTIVE_CONTINUITY_ABSENT.** This is not a readiness rating. It
says Nexus controls *turns* well and does not yet own *objectives*.

## 5. Product delta

Minimum workable Nexus for *finish reliably* versus today:

| Capability | Today | Minimum needed |
|---|---|---|
| Registered intent | first user message in a transcript; `title: "Task <id>"` | durable **objective record**: original request verbatim, deliverable kind (CHANGE / REPORT / VERDICT), required coverage, constraints, operator amendments, completion definition |
| Epoch continuity | turn end = objective end; `/clear` = total loss | on STEP_LIMIT / CAPACITY / repeated verifier rejection: persist consequences, materialise a fresh context, **continue the same objective** |
| Durable consequences | candidate identity, receipts, plan, milestones (good); everything else lives only in the transcript | add: findings / conclusions, ruled-out approaches, open questions, epoch dispositions. Changed files are derived from git/candidate identity, not from model claims. |
| Progress and stop | step count only | per-epoch progress signal (new diff, new receipt, new finding, plan advance) and **ABANDONED_BOUNDEDLY** after N non-progressing epochs or a budget, with a stated reason |
| Completion | model claim + verifier not failing | **reconciliation**: the objective record against observable reality (diff exists and is non-empty for CHANGE; a final report exists for REPORT/VERDICT; verifier not regressed vs baseline). The model's claim is only a candidate. |
| Uncontrolled failure | crashes and hangs largely fixed (D2–D4); **context death is still unrecovered** | context death becomes an epoch boundary |

Explicitly **not** in the minimum: parallel workstreams, dependency graphs, relational awareness across workstreams,
escalation tiers, LLM summarisation, turn-specific context planners. No evidence in the corpus shows a task that needed
them. The single-objective path does not complete yet.

## 7. Architectural options

### 7.1 Where objective continuity lives

| Option | For | Against | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **O1 Inside `runTurn`**: lift `maxSteps`, rebuild in place on block | smallest diff | `agent.ts` is 2.5k lines; the model in the loop stays completion authority; turn and objective concerns get mixed; reconciliation is hard to isolate or test | reject |
| **O2 Objective supervisor above `runTurn`**, in the ApplicationCore layer: loop of epochs over a durable objective record; each epoch is one `runTurn` on a materialised context | deterministic code outside the model; reuses `TurnResult` as the epoch result, `DurableStateManager`, `CandidateIdentity` and receipts; testable with a scripted client; the execution loop barely changes | the TUI path calls `runTurn` directly and must be wired later; adds a new persisted record | **preferred** |
| O3 Separate supervisor process or service | strong isolation | IPC, lifecycle and state sync for no current benefit | premature |
| O4 Work-graph orchestrator | addresses multi-workstream problems | no evidence that any task needs it; single-objective completion is unproven | premature (gate in section 8) |
| O5 Prior-art LLM summary compaction inside the loop | well-trodden | local-model summarisation failure modes (PRIOR-ART §6); does not create an objective layer | at most an ingredient later |

### 7.2 Context materialisation per epoch

| Option | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Resume the full transcript | That is today's behaviour; it reaches the same wall. |
| Current deterministic compaction | Verbatim memory; restart loops (F2, F3). |
| C2 references within the transcript | Sound for read-only phases; ends at the first mutation (K2). |
| **Deterministic projection from durable records**: system prompt, then objective record (verbatim request, plus deliverable and completion definition stated separately), then established consequences (git-derived diff summary, receipts, plan state, recorded findings, ruled-out list), then last-epoch tail | **Preferred.** It is what prior art converges on (store is truth, window is projection). Precedent: C2's "re-runnable reference" for observations; candidate identity for changes. |
| LLM summary of the prior epoch | Ingredient only, never the record. |

Design rules taken from evidence:
- **E4:** end the materialised context with state or evidence, or with a specific question. Never with a bare
  "continue the task" after fresh evidence.
- **K8:** present the operator's premise as a claim, separate from established facts. Keep that separation minimal now,
  because quality is not gating.

### 7.3 Escalation

The gateway has lead/deep pools, and Nexus has planner/coder routing hooks. Escalation fits naturally as a per-epoch
model choice made by the supervisor ("this epoch did not progress; run the next one on the deep tier"). It is a
**hypothesis** (U5): there is no Nexus evidence yet that a stronger tier converts W2/W3. It comes after the supervisor exists.

### 7.4 Completion reconciliation

Implement it as a deterministic check in the supervisor against the objective record:
- **CHANGE:** the candidate diff is non-empty and touches the declared scope, and the verifier has not regressed against
  baseline (bound to `CandidateIdentity`).
- **REPORT / VERDICT:** a final report artefact exists in the record.

The model's `task_completed` only triggers reconciliation. Finalisation (assembling the deliverable) stays trivial in this
phase: the diff or the report. Quality modifiers are out of scope.

## 8. Orchestration / work-graph assessment

Does Nexus need a broader orchestration capability? **Yes, the minimal form: one objective, serial epochs.** It does not
yet need the multi-workstream form.

Minimum responsibilities now:
1. Register and persist intent.
2. Run epochs.
3. Detect epoch boundaries from `TurnResult`.
4. Persist consequences.
5. Materialise the next epoch.
6. Measure progress.
7. Reconcile completion.
8. Stop as COMPLETED or ABANDONED_BOUNDEDLY.

| Concern | Now | Later |
|---|---|---|
| Dependencies / blockers | Record a blocker as a relation, *condition X blocks work Y*, on the objective record. With one workstream, `Blocked(A)` usually is `Blocked(objective)`, but the representation should not hard-code that. | Multi-workstream: `Blocked(A) ≠ Blocked(objective)` when other paths remain. |
| Coexistence / serialisation | Serial epochs. Concurrent read-only tool calls already exist inside a turn. | Two workstreams only when relations say CAN/SHOULD run concurrently (disjoint files, no verification dependency). An idle worker is correct otherwise. |
| Epistemic independence | Keep independent review outside Nexus (as practised). | An independent reviewer epoch with a clean context: a cheap version of "MUST_REMAIN_INDEPENDENT_OF". |
| Critical path | Trivial (single chain). | Needed only with a graph. |
| Resource allocation | Per-epoch step budget plus total objective budget. | Tier choice per epoch (escalation). |
| Dynamic replanning | A finding can amend the plan; an operator amendment is recorded on the objective. | Discoveries add or remove nodes. |

**Gate for the work-graph increment:** a dogfood objective, run under the supervisor, that fails or wastes material
budget specifically because it was not decomposed or parallelised. Until that exists, typed relation fields on durable
records (BLOCKED_BY, SATISFIES, SUPERSEDES, RULED_OUT_FOR, PRODUCES) give graph *semantics* without graph *machinery*.

### I1: Objective supervisor (the core increment)

- **Purpose:** an objective survives epoch boundaries and ends only as COMPLETED or ABANDONED_BOUNDEDLY.
